assumptions: The opportunity is assessed at planning stage, and absent contracts or cohorts are treated as material uncertainty rather than automatic proof of failure.
The exposure-register service stays outside accredited verification and does not assume access to supplier or verifier data for launch.
Customers will provide minimally usable customs and procurement extracts under a compliant processing agreement if they accept the engagement.
The founder can use contractors for methodology, legal and security review while maintaining the stated 15-20 hour weekly commitment.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Multiple prepaid implementations with above-threshold importers that document fee-exceeding value, actual sales-cycle and CAC, delivery hours, security costs, contribution margin, conversion to quarterly retainers and renewal; plus signed workflow/data agreements and comparative evidence that the register changes treasury decisions beyond what low-priced software or SAP provides.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Reframing the opportunity as a contracted treasury-control workflow rather than a broad SaaS product better matches the immediate cash exposure and identifies an obtainable operating position. It remains unproven that an independent register adds enough value beside existing software and ERP workflows.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Covered importers face a genuine certificate-budgeting obligation, and recurring variance review could be useful. No importer has paid for or signed the redesigned service, and proposed quarterly fees remain difficult to reconcile with a €2,500 annual substitute without evidence of superior decision value.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid implementation and quarterly work orders improve validation discipline, cash conversion and downside control, while shifting verification and supplier collection outside scope. Yet CAC, labor, security burden, contribution margins, renewal and payback are all planning assumptions, and the service-heavy model has lower operating leverage.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Above-threshold mid-market importers needing treasury support are a clearer initial segment than all CBAM users. The threshold narrows the pool, account counts remain unknown, and larger or sophisticated importers may already be served by internal teams or incumbent systems.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A lightweight independent control service can coexist with any ERP and may win accounts wanting rapid deployment or human review. However, it is nonexclusive, replaceable and easy for consultants, specialist vendors or incumbent platforms to imitate, limiting domination potential.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Repeated exposure-register work could extend into procurement scenarios, additional regulated materials, other EU markets and broader carbon-cost controls. Expansion becomes credible only if the initial service generates reusable templates, permissioned learning and customer trust.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Importer-specific histories and embedded quarterly routines could create modest switching costs, but the agreement is unsigned and proposed as nonexclusive and replaceable. Public regulatory inputs, customer-controlled data and readily copied service methods leave little durable protection.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The redesigned offer is faster to launch, requires fewer external dependencies and provides documented human-reviewed variance control rather than another full compliance stack. Its incremental performance, convenience and financial value versus inexpensive software or SAP have not been demonstrated.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Current certificate purchase exposure and recurring price updates create a strong near-term reason to establish budgeting controls. Competitive entry is accelerating at the same time, so the timing window may be short.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Direct account-based selling to a narrow list is more controllable than relying initially on referrals, and a fixed-scope implementation is a concrete entry offer. There is still no pipeline, conversion evidence, observed CAC or validated channel, and enterprise trust reviews may be difficult within part-time capacity.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The 45,000 PLN launch plan, customer-upload fallback, fixed scope and 15-20 weekly hours align better with the founder's capital and employment constraints. Material risks remain around data security, regulatory liability, enterprise sales, service standardization and sufficient value from defaults and importer records.

highest_value_structural_change: Convert the proposed replaceable service into a validated recurring treasury-control position by securing signed prepaid agreements that mandate quarterly use and produce permissioned variance histories, then standardize the work into a higher-leverage product layer.
main_structural_strength: The redesign removes supplier and verifier data as launch-critical dependencies and uses prepaid, fixed-scope delivery to test real demand with lower capital and better compatibility with the founder's constraints.
primary_score_limiter: The redesigned workflow position, pricing and recurring economics remain hypothetical, while inexpensive specialist software and SAP can cover much of the same customer need.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: A direct vendor already prices overlapping CBAM projection and procurement capabilities at €2,500 per year, SAP is adding cash-impact forecasting, and no importer has signed or paid for the proposed differentiated treasury-control service.
